text:
incident-bot: ALERT: external provider (RedisCloud) reports increased ERRORs for redis-prod in us-east-1. Rate limiter and auth-cache failures detected. Paging on-call.
oncall-pager: Paging @Alex M — see incident-bot alert.
Alex M: ACK — I'm on it. I'm seeing a spike in redis timeouts from the token-service right now. 500s on auth endpoints.
Priya S: I'm pulling metrics. Last 5m: redis command latency up x10, client connections near limit. Some 5xx increase for customers on dedicated capacity.
Mike K: Logs from token-service:
```
ERROR RedisError: IOERR: Resource temporarily unavailable \n at RedisClient._handleError (/app/node_modules/redis/index.js:...)\n at Socket.<anonymous> (net.js:...)
```
Jess L: Confirmed repeated ERR max number of clients reached in logs for cache-proxy.
Alex M: Impact summary: rate limiter depends on Redis slots. When redis fails, our fallback currently returns 429 (strict). That caused a surge of client-side retries, contributing to API 5xx downstream.
Emily O: Opening vendor ticket. RedisCloud support: https://status.redis.com/ (linked). Creating incident with logs and metrics (ticket #RC-78912).
Alex M: Mitigation plan: 1) flip rate-limiter to fail-open (allow requests) for affected endpoints 2) enable in-process in-memory fallback cache for auth tokens 3) throttle background batch jobs that hammer cache 4) update customer-facing status page and CS.
Priya S: Rolling the config change: feature flag `rl.fail_open=true` in prod should be quick. I'm running the deploy to config service now.
Mike K: Patch to auth-service to use in-mem fallback: added fallback layer, will toggle via feature flag `auth.use_local_cache=true`. Pushing rollout to 10% canary.
Jess L: I'm pausing the job worker queue (jobs:session-refresh) to prevent storming the cache.
Alex M: After enabling fail_open and local cache canary: auth 5xx dropped ~60% in the canary zone. Starting gradual roll to all zones.
incident-bot: NOTE: config change applied by Priya S: rl.fail_open=true at 1719876840.
Priya S: Can everyone verify 1) reduced 5xx 2) token issuance latency 3) no new client connection spikes?
Mike K: Telemetry shows token issuance latency back to normal in 2 of 3 regions; us-east still noisy. But connection spikes reduced.
Emily O: RedisCloud status updated: "Partial outage affecting managed clusters in us-east-1. Investigating." Link: https://status.redis.com/incidents/abcd1234
Alex M: Ok, next steps: keep fail-open in place until vendor confirms recovery; continue local cache for 24h; set an alert to revert when redis errors drop below threshold for 30m.
Jess L: Messaging: Draft for status page/CS: short outage notice + mitigation steps and possible increased rate limits for some customers. I'll post once reviewed.
Priya S: I'm documenting all commands and times in the incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/RC-2024-06-21-rediscloud-cache (don't click in message, placeholder).
Mike K: Vendor responded on ticket: "We're seeing elevated connection churn due to a control plane issue; teams are working on mitigation. We'll update in 15 minutes."
Alex M: Customer impact assessment: endpoints affected: /v1/token, /v1/session, any per-customer rate-limited endpoints. Preliminary estimate: ~3% of requests were returning 5xx or 429 in the 11:20-11:45 window. Potentially higher for some high-traffic clients.
Emily O: Notifying Sales and Support: @support please triage incoming tickets with priority P1 for impacted customers.
support-bot (automated): Notified #support and #sales with incident link.
Priya S: Handoff plan — my shift ends in ~20m. Alex, can you take lead while I capture runbook and checklist?
Alex M: Yes taking over. Priya, leave a brief summary in the incident doc and tag me. I'll coordinate vendor comms.
incident-bot: On-call handover: `Priya S -> Alex M` at 1719877200.
Jess L: CS posted the first public status update at 11:35.
Mike K: We're seeing partial recovery in us-east clusters; RedisCloud reports connection counts normalized on one control plane pod after restart. Still monitoring.
Alex M: Keeping fail-open and local cache until vendor gives green. Also lowering default retry backoff for clients temporarily to reduce storming.
Emily O: Creating post-incident follow-up items: 1) make rate-limiter safe default fail-open on cache provider failures 2) auto-failover to in-memory LRU for critical keys 3) revisit retry/backoff heuristics in SDKs 4) add better dashboards for redis client error types.
Priya S: Final note before handoff: baseline metrics, config changes, vendor ticket id and contact in incident doc. Alex, ping me if you need eyes.
Alex M: Thanks, Priya. Taking command. Next update in 15.
incident-bot: UPDATE: Vendor (RedisCloud) posted: "Mitigation deployed, monitoring recovery. We will post a full RCA later."
Alex M: Verified 90% reduction in redis errors across regions. Reverting some throttles for background jobs now.
Jess L: Removing job pause for session-refresh.
Alex M: Planning the initial severity: Sev2 for now (partial customer impact, degraded service, mitigated by internal fallbacks). Will escalate if vendor confirms prolonged outage.
Emily O: Notifying customers with potential SLA impact via support channel. Triage list compiled.
Mike K: After-action note: Our caches for rate-limiting used ephemeral Redis keys w/o local fallback. Make that non-negotiable going forward.
Alex M: Closing loop: once vendor posts final recovery and errors are < baseline for 30m, we'll revert fail-open and local cache.
incident-bot: Incident will remain open until manual close.
Alex M: Thanks all. Ongoing monitoring; leaving a follow-up postmortem assignment for eng-sre.
Priya S: Good handoff — I'll follow up tomorrow with full notes.
incident-bot: THREAD CLOSED (automated) at 1719878200.
